UPSTREAM: drivers/usb/acpi: Add a driver for generating USB ACPI Add a support for generating USB port descriptors for ACPI based on their definition by the board in devicetree.cb. This will generate a _UPC and _PLD for each port, using a generic _PLD by default. The _PLD can also be customized for more accurate descriptions if necessary. UPSTREAM: soc/intel: Add support for USB ACPI code generation To support generating USB devices in ACPI the platform needs to know how to determine a device name for each USB port, and for any root hubs that may be present. Recent Intel platforms route all ports to an XHCI controller through a root hub. This is supported by considering the root hub to be USB port type 0, the USB 2.0 ports to be type 2, and the USB 3.0 ports to be type 3. This was tested with a Kaby Lake platform by adding entries to the devicetree and checking the resulting SSDT. UPSTREAM: soc/amd/stoneyridge: Support ACPI USB code generation To support generating USB devices in ACPI the platform needs to know how to determine a device name for each USB port, and for any root hubs that may be present. The AMD Stoney Ridge platform has separate controllers for USB 2.0 and USB 3.0. The USB 2.0 ports are connected through a hub to an EHCI controller while the USB 3.0 ports are directly connected to the xHCI controller. This topology is described in ACPI and the port names are exposed by the soc_acpi_name() function. The USB controllers are configured to scan for static USB devices in the devicetree and use the soc_acpi_name() function to identify them. Add programatic support for minijail '-G' flag to ProcessManager This CL is in preparation to run the shill process tree as a non-root user. Shill will soon spawn openvpn as user/group 'shill' before openvpn drops to user/group 'openvpn'. Startup process for openvpn needs write access to /dev/net/tun, which requires making shill user part of the 'tun' group and allowing the jailed openvpn process to inherit the supplementary groups from the 'shill' UID before dropping to 'openvpn'. Unfortunately, adding this single flag pushed the number of args in the ProcessManager:SpawnProcessInMinijailWithPipes function to 11, which is effectively prevented by gMock code, which only allows for mocking functions that use up to 10 arguments. Hence, this code also refactors the function to take in a struct with the 3 standard file descriptors instead of passing them each individually as arguments.
